selected_assets.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: selected cinematic MASTER STILL for a connected basement workshop arrival video concept. One photorealistic scene, not a collage, board, UI or video.
STRICT VEHICLE IDENTITY INPUTS: use all five supplied all-angle reference sheets as the vehicle geometry authority, including their rear views. Image 1 = corrected old rounded Mitsubishi Lancer with narrow swept clear headlamps, slim upper grille, small standard rims. Image 2 = black first-generation Chevrolet Cruze. Image 3 = burgundy Toyota Camry. Image 4 = dark black/navy BOXY Jeep Cherokee KK with vertical rectangular headlights and chrome seven-slot grille. Image 5 = approved 2011-era Ford Explorer with flowing rounded body, black rear-quarter pillar treatment, wraparound/T-shaped rear lamps, stock multi-spoke wheels and three-bar FRONT grille. Do not replace any model with a generic generation. In particular Explorer is NOT the old 2006 box with stacked square rear lamps; Lancer is NOT modern shark-nose/Evo and must retain the corrected sheet's swept narrow headlights.
SCENE: a spacious professional UNDERGROUND BASEMENT automobile workshop in Maracaibo, unmistakably below ground. Low flat concrete ceiling with deep concrete beams and orderly exposed utility pipes, substantial concrete support columns around the perimeter, clean ceiling LED strips, white walls with navy lower wall band and one thin lime accent. Matte gray concrete floor and natural tire contact shadows. No aboveground windows, no steel-truss warehouse, no skylights, no outdoor panorama. Neat tool cabinets/service bays sit against the far-side perimeter, never hiding cars. Bright usable neutral LED illumination with gentle warm late-afternoon light reaching down the entrance ramp from BEHIND the camera. No black/gold luxury theme.
ARRIVAL AND CAMERA: a broad clearly DOWNWARD-SLOPING concrete vehicle access ramp enters from behind/upper-left camera and descends to this basement floor. Show the slope, ramp side retaining wall and bottom transition in the immediate left foreground so the basement descent is clear. Camera at roughly driver-window height, beside/slightly behind the driver side of the incoming SILVER 2011-era Explorer. The silver Explorer is foreground LEFT with its nose pointing inward/down the ramp INTO the workshop, away from the exit and camera. We see its approved rear-driver-side three-quarter body with correct wraparound/T-shaped tail lamps and lowered front driver window ready for the camera to enter. Keep enough of its side visible to identify it, but compose it mainly in the lower-left foreground so it does NOT obscure any parked car.
EIGHT VEHICLES TOTAL. Exactly ONE incoming silver Explorer plus EXACTLY SEVEN parked cars ahead. Set a wide clear central aisle ending in a gently staggered shallow arc of SEVEN separate parked vehicles, all their FRONTS facing the incoming Explorer/camera. Every parked vehicle must have its whole front and distinct body silhouette readable, with clear physical gaps and no overlaps/column obstructions. Exact left-to-right order of the SEVEN:
1. TAUPE corrected old Lancer from image 1.
2. BLACK Cruze from image 2.
3. BURGUNDY Camry from image 3.
4. DARK BLACK/NAVY boxy Cherokee KK from image 4.
5. WHITE Explorer: exactly the SAME 2011-era body/wheels as image 5, changing only silver paint to white.
6. SILVER Lancer: exactly the SAME corrected body/headlights/grille/wheels as image 1, changing only taupe paint to silver.
7. DARK BLUE Lancer: exactly the SAME corrected body/headlights/grille/wheels as image 1, changing only taupe paint to dark blue.
Do not omit any of the three Lancers or confuse the white parked Explorer with the silver incoming one. Each car faces the camera with only gentle quarter angles. Make the room wide enough for all seven to be separate, readable and physically plausible. Foreground Explorer does not block parked Lancer #1. Clear aisle remains between incoming vehicle and parked arc.
CINEMATOGRAPHY: 16:9 landscape, high resolution approximately 2560×1440, ground-level wide-angle professional automotive photography with straight verticals, crisp cars, realistic material texture and balanced exposure. No people, no driver, no hands, no visible drone, no extra vehicles, no additional parked silver Explorer, no text overlays, no signs, no HUD, no UI, no decorative typography, no standalone logos. Natural ordinary vehicle badges only. Prioritize count, exact sheet identities and simple connected spatial layout over decoration. Produce exactly ONE master image.

reference_note: All five corrected angle sheets were physically inspected and supplied to the basement master. The connected interior uses the selected master plus four supporting sheets because the tool permits at most five image paths; the Camry is carried through the selected master.
